title: STROLLANE · NYC — street-level 12 Experience Dimensions
area_label: Manhattan (LION borocode 1 incl. Roosevelt & Randalls Is.)
comparison_scope: Percentiles are ranked among the 10,533 segments of this area (Manhattan (LION borocode 1 incl. Roosevelt & Randalls Is.)).
score_method: Each scored indicator → percentile rank 0–100 among segments of the comparison area that have a value (ties take the lowest rank; "lower is better" indicators reversed as 100 − rank). Dimension score = equal-weight mean of the indicator percentiles available on that segment. N/A when none is available; missing values are never 0. Validation/context indicators never enter a score.

indicators.label: Weighted landmark proximity
indicators.method: Sample the street centerline every 40 m. For LPC landmark lots within 300 m, apply Gaussian distance weights (σ = 100 m) and average all samples. Higher values indicate stronger exposure to recognized landmarks.
notes: Distance is to the landmark lot polygon (0 inside the lot); each lot (incl. multi-part lots) counted once per sample.

indicators.label: Recorded trees
indicators.method: Count mapped tree points within 30 m of each street segment. Divide by segment length in kilometres, using a minimum length of 80 m to avoid inflated short-segment values. Higher values mean denser recorded tree presence.
notes: Each tree is assigned to its single nearest walkable segment within 30 m so trees at corners are not double-counted.
sources: NYC Parks Forestry Tree Points (structure = Full)

indicators.label: Park adjacency
indicators.method: Sample points along the street centerline and side offsets at 20 m and 40 m. Divide points inside official park polygons by all valid sample points. Higher values indicate stronger spatial adjacency to park land.
notes: Samples every 20 m at offsets 0, ±20, ±40 m.

indicators.label: Tree-canopy cover
indicators.method: Create a 20 m buffer on both sides of the street and intersect it with the 2021 land-cover raster. Divide canopy-class pixel area by total valid classified area × 100. Higher values indicate more overhead tree cover.
notes: Spec requires the TNC / UVM 2021 land-cover raster. It is not in the repo, and NYC Open Data only publishes the 2017 edition (he6d-2qns, 6-in, 1.33 GB zip). The 2017 raster is not substituted for the 2021 one. N/A until the 2021 raster is supplied.
sources: NYC Land Cover 2021 (6 in) — TNC / UVM Spatial Analysis Lab

indicators.label: Cultural POI proximity
indicators.method: Map museums, galleries, theatres, libraries, and similar cultural destinations. For locations within 450 m, sum Gaussian distance-decay weights (σ = 150 m) along the street. Higher values indicate stronger nearby cultural access.
notes: 818 cultural POIs (museum, gallery, theatre, arts centre, cinema, library, music venue, concert hall).

indicators.label: Noise-complaint intensity
indicators.method: Filter geolocated NYC 311 noise complaints to the latest 12 months. Sum Gaussian distance weights for reports within 150 m (σ = 50 m), then reverse the percentile. Fewer nearby complaints rank higher.
notes: 177034 geolocated noise complaints in the 12-month window.

indicators.label: Roadway width
indicators.method: Read roadway width in feet from NYC LION for each street segment. Convert values to Manhattan-relative percentiles and reverse them so narrower streets rank higher. This is a quietness proxy, not a measured sound level.
notes: N/A where LION records no roadway width (common on park paths and step streets).

indicators.label: Mapped sidewalk coverage
indicators.method: Sample roughly every 20 m along the street and add left/right offsets at 5, 8, 11, and 14 m. Divide points inside mapped sidewalk polygons by all valid points. Higher values indicate wider or more continuous sidewalk coverage.
notes: N/A on park paths and step streets (LION types 6, 7): they have no curbside sidewalk to measure.

indicators.label: Walking distance to seating
indicators.method: Locate public seating points on the walkable network. From each street midpoint, calculate the shortest walking distance to the nearest seat, capped at 500 m. Shorter distances indicate easier access to rest.
notes: 1191 of 1194 Manhattan seats linked to the OSM pedestrian network (≤100 m snap).
Midpoint joins the network at its nearest walk-graph node; values ≥ 500 m are capped at 500.

indicators.label: Pedestrian-ramp coverage
indicators.method: Identify evaluable pedestrian crossing nodes along the street. Check whether at least one recorded curb ramp lies within 20 m of each node, then divide covered nodes by all eligible nodes. Higher values mean more documented ramp provision.
notes: Eligible nodes = segment end nodes joining ≥3 walkable segments, at least one a roadway (a crossing). N/A when a segment has no eligible crossing node.

indicators.label: POI diversity × quantity
indicators.method: Collect OSM places within 150 m of the street midpoint and group them by activity type. Compute normalized Shannon diversity H and multiply it by ln(1 + POI count). Higher values indicate both more places and greater use diversity.
notes: H = Shannon entropy of activity types ÷ ln(number of types present) (0–1).

indicators.label: Observed pedestrian flow
indicators.method: Standardize pedestrian-sensor observations by hour and period to make locations comparable. Use the median valid hourly pedestrian count and compare it with the POI-based vibrancy model. This is validation evidence, not a full-street score.
notes: 36 segments carry one of 36 Manhattan DOT count locations (snapped ≤ 30 m). Rate = period total ÷ hours (weekday 7–9 AM, 4–7 PM; Saturday 12–2 PM), median of valid periods in the 4 most recent rounds (Oct 2024 – May 2026). Validation evidence only — never part of a street score.

indicators.label: Food and retail proximity
indicators.method: Extract mapped restaurants, cafés, bars, shops, and other retail POIs. At street samples, sum Gaussian proximity values for locations within 150 m (σ = 50 m). Higher values indicate stronger nearby food and retail availability.
notes: 20934 food, drink and shop POIs.

indicators.label: Scenic POI proximity
indicators.method: Select OSM viewpoints, public art, fountains, memorials, and monuments. Compute Gaussian distance weights within 300 m (σ = 100 m) along street samples. Higher values indicate greater proximity to scenic features.
notes: 1432 viewpoints, artworks, fountains, memorials and monuments.

indicators.label: Walking distance to waterfront
indicators.method: Verify public waterfront entries and their links to walkable paths. Calculate the shortest pedestrian-network route from each street midpoint to the nearest valid entrance. Shorter distances indicate easier public access to waterfront views.
notes: 672 valid entrances: connected walk-graph nodes inside public waterfront space (open WPAA or a park within 30 m of river/bay) and within 60 m of open water. Capped at 3000 m.

indicators.label: Connected junctions
indicators.method: Construct the walkable-road topology from NYC LION segments. Identify junctions meeting at least three segments and count those within 250 m of each street midpoint. Higher counts indicate more route choices and connections.
notes: 5041 LION junctions (≥3 walkable segments).

indicators.label: Walking-network detour
indicators.method: Sample feasible nearby origin–destination pairs around each street. Divide the shortest pedestrian-network distance by straight-line distance and take the median. Ratios closer to 1 indicate less detour and more direct walking.
notes: Origin = walk-graph node nearest the midpoint; destinations = node closest to 375 m in each 45° sector of the 250–500 m ring; pairs unreachable within 1.5 km excluded; N/A with fewer than 3 feasible pairs.

indicators.label: Pedestrian-injury crash intensity
indicators.method: Filter three years of reported collisions involving pedestrian injury or death. Sum Gaussian proximity weights for crash points within 120 m (σ = 40 m) and reverse the percentile. Fewer nearby crashes rank higher.
notes: 4204 pedestrian-injury/fatal crashes in the 3-year window. Not adjusted for pedestrian volume.

indicators.label: Crime-report proximity
indicators.method: Combine NYPD historic and current-YTD complaint records, deduplicate incident IDs, and retain felony and misdemeanor cases. Sum Gaussian weights for reports within 300 m (σ = 100 m). Fewer reports rank higher, but this remains a proxy rather than personal risk.
notes: 171188 felony + misdemeanor complaint reports. Report density is a proxy, not personal risk.
sources: NYPD Complaint Data Historic (qgea-i56i) + Current YTD (5uac-w243)

indicators.label: Distance to highways/ramps
indicators.method: Measure straight-line distance from each street midpoint to the nearest mapped highway or access ramp. Cap distances at 1,500 m and rank farther distances higher. This acts as a proximity-based environmental exposure proxy.
notes: 1414 LION expressway / ramp centerlines (types 2, 9).

indicators.label: Impervious surface cover
indicators.method: Buffer each street by 20 m on both sides and overlay the 2021 classified land-cover raster. Divide impervious-surface area by total valid raster area × 100. Lower values indicate less nearby hard-surface cover.
notes: Same TNC / UVM 2021 land-cover raster as canopy_pct; not acquired, not substituted. N/A.
sources: NYC Land Cover 2021 (6 in) — TNC / UVM Spatial Analysis Lab

indicators.label: Annual NO₂ area context
indicators.method: Read annual NO₂ concentration using the official DOHMH geography, period, and source units. Use this only as neighbourhood-scale environmental context; do not assign the value directly to individual street segments.
notes: Annual mean NO₂ 2024 (ppb) by Community District, DOHMH NYCCAS. Shown as a neighbourhood-scale context layer; the value is deliberately NOT assigned to street segments and never scored.
sources: NYC DOHMH Air Quality (NYCCAS annual NO₂)

indicators.label: Entry-permitted subway entrances
indicators.method: Keep only MTA entrances that allow passengers to enter. Count qualifying entrances within 400 m of each street midpoint. Higher values indicate more nearby access points, not higher service frequency.
notes: 840 entry-permitted entrances.
sources: MTA Subway Entrances and Exits: 2024 (entry allowed)

indicators.label: Distance to subway entrance
indicators.method: From each street midpoint, find the nearest MTA entrance that permits boarding access. Measure distance, cap it at 1,500 m, and reverse the Manhattan percentile. Shorter distances indicate stronger subway proximity.
sources: MTA Subway Entrances and Exits: 2024 (entry allowed)

qa.excluded_types: 2 highway, 3 bridge, 4 tunnel, 9 ramp, 13/14 ferry & other non-walkable

trees.label: NYC Parks Forestry Tree Points (structure = Full)

tnc_landcover.label: NYC Land Cover 2021 (6 in) — TNC / UVM Spatial Analysis Lab

qa.retrieved_via: Socrata API /resource/cqsj-cfgu.json?borough=Manhattan from the user's desktop browser (processing sandboxes cannot reach data.cityofnewyork.us)

qa.filter: pedestrians injured > 0 OR pedestrians killed > 0, borough = MANHATTAN

nypd_complaints.label: NYPD Complaint Data Historic (qgea-i56i) + Current YTD (5uac-w243)

qa.dedup: historic + YTD merged on complaint number (cmplnt_num) when the store was built

qa.filter: feat_code 2620 (river) / 2660 (bay, channel); ponds and reservoirs excluded

dohmh_no2.label: NYC DOHMH Air Quality (NYCCAS annual NO₂)

subway.label: MTA Subway Entrances and Exits: 2024 (entry allowed)

id_scheme: segment_id = "MN-" + LION physicalid (+ "-n" when several LION records share one), identical to data/manhattan-streets.json.

urban_vibrancy_vs_ped_flow.note: Rank correlation between DOT observed people/hour and the POI-based vibrancy model at count locations. DOT locations are mostly busy retail corridors, so the range is restricted.

value_note: Scores are relative ranks within the comparison area, not calibrated experience scores. N/A = not measurable, never 0.
